quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Some customer email addresses were exposed by mistake. Write to the affected customers. The message must tell them what happened, what to watch for, and what you are doing.
options: Subject: Important: a security incident affecting your email address

Dear customer,

On 9 September, a mistake in one of our mailings exposed your email address to other recipients. No passwords or payment details were involved.

If you have questions, please call 0800 000 2222.

We sincerely apologise.

Yours sincerely,
Vesna Voss, Customer Director

You may receive more spam or suspicious messages, so please do not click links in emails you do not expect. We have corrected the fault, and we are reporting the incident to the data protection authority.
quests.hint: Customers want to know if they are at risk and what to do. Technical detail can wait.
quests.explanation: For affected customers, what happened and what it means for them matter most. Practical advice and a contact route come before the apology and any organisational detail.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The same incident: write to the data protection regulator. Frame: Subject: Personal data breach notification: Harbourline Ltd, 9 September / Greeting: Dear Sir or Madam, / Sign-off: Yours faithfully, Vesna Voss. Put together the body.
options: A mailing was sent with recipients' addresses visible, affecting 1,860 customers; no passwords or financial data were included.
We will provide a full report within seven days and can supply further details on request.
We have recalled what we could, corrected the mailing process and informed the affected individuals today.
We are notifying you of a personal data breach that occurred on 9 September and was discovered at 2:30 pm the same day.
quests.hint: Regulators need facts in a standard order: what, when, how many, what data, what you did.
quests.explanation: A regulator reads for compliance, so scale, data type and remedial steps are essential. Committing to a full report shows cooperation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The same incident: write to staff. Frame: Subject: Data incident on 9 September: what you need to do / Greeting: Dear colleagues, / Sign-off: Thank you, Vesna. Arrange the body.
options: If a customer contacts you, use the approved script on the intranet and log the call in the incident tracker.
We will brief you on Friday at 10 am, and thank you for your discretion.
A mailing to customers on 9 September exposed some email addresses, and the incident is now being handled by a response team.
Please do not discuss it on social media or with journalists, and send any press or customer enquiries to communications@example.com.
quests.hint: Employees need to know what to say, what not to say, and where to send questions.
quests.explanation: Staff messages focus on behaviour. Clear rules and resources reduce risk of misinformation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Draft services agreement: proposed change to clause 8 (liability) / Dear Mr Tanaka, / Yours sincerely, Caroline Seddon). Arrange the body.
options: We would propose limiting liability to the fees paid in the previous twelve months, which is standard in our sector.
Thank you for sending the draft agreement, and we are keen to move ahead.
We are unable to accept clause 8 as written, because it makes us liable for all indirect losses, which we cannot insure.
If you agree, we can sign this month.
quests.hint: Positive intent, the problem clause with a reason, a specific alternative, a benefit for agreeing.
quests.explanation: Explaining the reason (insurance) shows that the objection is practical, not tactical. A specific alternative and a prospect of signing move the negotiation forward.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Confirmation of changed scope: Phase 2 of the Zephyr project / Dear Ms Nunez, / Kind regards, Damian Shaw). Arrange the body.
options: Following our call on Tuesday, I am writing to confirm the change to Phase 2, which we agreed verbally.
Could you reply to confirm that you agree.
We will add the customer portal, which is not in the original quote, and this adds £6,500 and two weeks to the timetable, so the new end date is 26 September.
So that we can begin on Monday?
quests.hint: Written confirmation of verbal changes protects both sides.
quests.explanation: Putting agreed changes in writing prevents later disputes. The impact on price and date must be explicit, and asking for a reply creates the record.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Request for a written explanation: price increase on contract 7715 / Dear Ms Petrov, / Yours sincerely, Jonas Reuter). Arrange the body.
options: Our contract includes a fixed price until December, and clause 4 permits increases only where raw material costs change by more than 10%.
Thank you for letting us know that prices will increase by 12% from 1 October.
We would like to review it before responding.
Could you send us a written breakdown of the costs that justify the increase?
quests.hint: Acknowledge, cite the contract, ask for evidence, state what you'll do.
quests.explanation: The contract clause makes it a legitimate request for evidence. Saying you will review it before responding avoids agreeing or refusing prematurely.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A project has gone badly wrong, and you must tell the client honestly and propose a recovery. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Project Meridian: where we are and how we propose to recover / Dear Ms Underhill, / Yours sincerely, Philip Hayes). Arrange the body.
options: I want to be direct: the project is eight weeks behind, and the launch on 1 November is no longer realistic.
May I visit you on Thursday to go through the plan?
The main causes are that we underestimated the integration work, and that requirements changed twice.
I propose a reduced first release on 1 December with the essential features, followed by the remaining features in February, and we will add three engineers at our own cost.
quests.hint: Honest summary, causes without blame-shifting, a specific recovery plan, a request to meet.
quests.explanation: The honest opening builds credibility. Owning the estimate and mentioning the changes fairly avoids defensiveness, and investing extra resources shows commitment.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Project Meridian recovery plan / Dear Mr Hayes, / Yours sincerely, Rina Underhill). Arrange the body.
options: I would agree to the 1 December date if the payment module is included, and we can move some reporting features to February.
Thank you for your honesty; it is much better to hear this now than in October.
Could we meet on Thursday to agree the scope? I will bring my product lead.
I cannot accept a first release without the payment module, since that is what our customers need.
quests.hint: Appreciate honesty, state the essential requirement, propose a trade-off.
quests.explanation: The client praises openness, sets a non-negotiable and proposes a trade. This keeps the partnership alive while protecting what matters.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Request for two additional engineers for Project Meridian / Dear Mr Winterbourne, / Kind regards, Philip Hayes). Arrange the body.
options: The project is eight weeks late, and the client has agreed to a revised date of 1 December.
Without extra help, we will miss it, which risks the £400,000 contract and the relationship.
The cost is about £48,000, and I can show you the plan on Wednesday.
I am asking for two additional engineers for Project Meridian for the next ten weeks.
quests.hint: State the request with numbers, the stakes, the cost, and the next step.
quests.explanation: The request is first, and the stakes are quantified. Seeing the cost against the contract value helps a director judge the trade-off.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A colleague is returning after a long illness. Assemble the email from her manager.
options: Dear Wanjiru,

Your workload will be lighter for the first two weeks, and we have moved your Tuesday meeting so that you can start gently. Please let me know if anything would help, and do not feel you must catch up at once.

Warmest wishes,
Michael
Subject: Welcome back on Monday
We're all delighted that you are coming back on Monday.
quests.hint: Welcome, practical adjustments, permission to ask for help.
quests.explanation: A returning colleague needs to feel welcome and not pressured. Practical adjustments show care without focusing on her illness.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Just checking in / Hi Sami, / Best, Edie). Arrange the body.
options: I hope you don't mind me writing.
No need to reply straight away.
I'm happy to take on a couple of your smaller tasks this week, and I'm free for a coffee if you'd like to talk.
I noticed you've been working late a lot, and I wanted to see how you are.
quests.hint: Show that you care, make a concrete offer, reduce pressure to answer.
quests.explanation: A gentle, low-pressure check-in respects the person's privacy. Offering specific help is more useful than 'let me know'.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: A personal matter I'd like to talk to you about / Dear Mr Bamford, / Kind regards, Ann-Marie Coyle). Arrange the body.
options: I am not asking you to change anything yet.
But I wanted you to hear it from me.
I would like to let you know that I am going through a difficult time at home, and I'm worried it may affect my work over the next few weeks.
Could we speak privately on Thursday?
quests.hint: Be brief, don't over-share, and ask for a private conversation.
quests.explanation: You can share only what you feel comfortable sharing. Requesting a private talk is a mature way to raise something sensitive.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: You have seen figures being changed in a report to hide a loss. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Confidential: concern about figures in the Q2 management report / Dear Ms Talbot, / Yours sincerely, Danielle Ng). Arrange the body.
options: On 14 July, I saw that the loss on the Norwich contract, shown as £62,000 in the draft, was changed to a £6,200 loss in the final version, and I could not find an explanation.
I would like to know how to proceed and whether I can be protected as someone raising a concern.
I have not discussed this with anyone else.
I would like to raise a confidential concern about the Q2 management report.
quests.hint: Confidentiality, facts without accusations, what you want to know.
quests.explanation: The email states what you saw, not what you believe others intended. Asking about protection shows awareness of the process.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Your confidential concern / Dear Ms Ng, / Yours sincerely, Helena Talbot). Arrange the body.
options: I will contact you again by 25 July, and you are protected under our whistleblowing policy, attached.
I will review the documents you mention, and I will need to ask Finance for the drafts, without naming you.
Thank you for raising this with me; you were right to do so, and I will treat your message in strict confidence.
Please keep any notes safe and avoid discussing it with colleagues.
quests.hint: Thank, explain the process, set expectations, protect.
quests.explanation: A compliance officer must reassure without promising an outcome. Giving a date for the next contact and citing the policy gives structure.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the email in which you tell your manager that you cannot sign a document you believe is inaccurate.
options: Dear Mr Dalton,
Subject: Unable to sign the safety certificate for Line 3
I am not able to sign the safety certificate for Line 3 as it stands.

The inspection of the guard rails scheduled for 10 June has not been carried out, and I cannot certify something I have not checked. I can sign as soon as the inspection is done, and I am available to help arrange it this week.

Kind regards,
Ifeanyi Obi
quests.hint: State the refusal, the reason, and the condition for change.
quests.explanation: A clear reason grounded in professional duty is hard to argue with. Saying when you can sign shows you are cooperating.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Put together the email arranging a call across London, Mumbai and San Francisco, avoiding local holidays.
options: I would like to arrange a one-hour call about the joint proposal, and I have tried to avoid local public holidays and early or late hours.

The two options are Tuesday 15 July at 2 pm London, 6:30 pm Mumbai and 6 am San Francisco, or Wednesday 16 July at 4 pm London, 8:30 pm Mumbai and 8 am San Francisco.

Could you tell me which you prefer, and if neither works, please suggest two alternatives?

Kind regards,
Marisol Vega
Dear all,
Subject: Proposed call times: 15 to 17 July (London, Mumbai and San Francisco)
quests.hint: Purpose, options with all time zones, action requested.
quests.explanation: Showing all zones prevents errors and proves fairness. Asking for two alternatives makes it easier to reach agreement.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Request to reschedule interview from 21 April to another date / Dear Ms Aziz, / Yours sincerely, Naveed Iqbal). Arrange the body.
options: I appreciate the inconvenience and am flexible on the time.
Thank you for the invitation to an interview on 21 April.
That day is Eid for me, and I would like to attend the celebrations with my family.
Could the interview take place on 22 or 23 April instead?
quests.hint: Thank, state the reason plainly, offer alternatives.
quests.explanation: You are not required to over-explain religious reasons. Offering alternative dates shows commitment to the process.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Lay out an email that cancels a group meeting and gathers availability for a new one.
options:
Could you fill in the poll below with your availability for Monday to Wednesday next week by 5 pm today? I'll confirm the new time this evening.

Thanks for your flexibility,
Hiro
Hi everyone,
I'm sorry, but tomorrow's 10 am meeting is cancelled because two key people are unavailable.
Subject: Tomorrow's meeting cancelled; please share availability for next week
quests.hint: State the cancellation first, then the action and deadline.
quests.explanation: People should know at once that the meeting won't happen. A same-day deadline and promise of confirmation let plans move quickly.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: An email thread has turned tense, with five people copied. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Late shipment: proposal for next steps / Dear all, / Kind regards, Bernadette). Arrange the body.
options: Thank you for all your messages.
To avoid further confusion, I suggest that the two of us most involved, Carla and Hussein, speak by phone today and share a short summary with everyone afterwards.
In the meantime, the replacement shipment will leave on Thursday, and I will confirm the tracking number as soon as I have it.
I can see that everyone wants to get this right.
quests.hint: Acknowledge everyone, propose a calmer channel, give the concrete facts.
quests.explanation: Suggesting a call reduces the heat that written exchanges create. Giving facts about the shipment keeps the message useful.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Set out the email in which you remove people from a thread and explain politely.
options: To keep things simple, I will continue this conversation with Anders and Zola only.
Dear all,
Subject: Moving this discussion to a smaller group

The rest of you have been copied so far for information, and I will send a short summary on Friday. Please let me know if you would like to stay on the thread.

Best wishes,
Torsten
quests.hint: State the change, reassure the others, provide an option.
quests.explanation: Explaining why people are removed avoids anyone feeling excluded. The offer to stay on the thread gives them control.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Structure an email replying to a message that was sent in anger by a client.
options:
I would like to call you today to go through what went wrong and agree the fastest fix. Please tell me the best number and time, and in the meantime I have asked our engineer to give the case top priority.

Yours sincerely,
Xiomara Torres
Subject: Re: This is unacceptable
I have read your message carefully, and I understand how frustrating the last three weeks have been.
Dear Mr Stanton,
quests.hint: Do not defend yourself in writing; offer a call and a first action.
quests.explanation: A phone call shows commitment and avoids escalating the written dispute. Immediate action shows you have taken the complaint seriously.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Your director has asked you to approve an invoice you have not verified. Build the diplomatic refusal.
options: Subject: Re: Approval of invoice 8850
Dear Ms Whitaker,

I am not able to approve invoice 8850 until I have checked it against the delivery note, which I have asked the warehouse to send. I expect to complete the check by tomorrow at noon and will approve it then if everything matches.

Kind regards,
Oluwafemi Aro
Thank you for your message, and I understand that the supplier needs to be paid promptly.
quests.hint: Understand her need, state the limit, provide a timetable.
quests.explanation: You refuse to bypass the control but not to help. Giving a time for completion shows that the delay is minimal.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A senior manager asks you to attend a meeting during your approved leave. Arrange your reply.
options: Dear Mr Beck,
Thank you for thinking of me for the meeting on 14 July, and I understand that it is important.

I am on leave from 7 to 18 July, which was approved in March, and I am travelling abroad. I can send a briefing note to Chloe before I go and be available for a fifteen-minute call by phone if there is an emergency.

Kind regards,
Annabel Fry
Subject: Re: Meeting on 14 July
quests.hint: Appreciate the request, state the constraint, offer a limited alternative.
quests.explanation: Referring to approved leave makes the refusal objective. A briefing note and limited availability show goodwill.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Request to lead the pension review / Dear Ms Okoro, / Kind regards, Piers Hess). Arrange the body.
options: Thank you for offering me the chance to lead the pension review.
I would be glad to support the project by preparing the data.
I am flattered that you thought of me.
However, I do not have the actuarial experience the review requires, and I think that the outcome would be better under someone with that background.
quests.hint: Thank, decline honestly, offer a limited contribution.
quests.explanation: Being honest about your limits protects the project. Offering to help with data shows willingness.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Feedback on your draft chapter / Dear Tomasz, / Best wishes, Dr Cecilia Bianchi). Arrange the body.
options: The argument in section two is very promising.
I suggest that you write a one-page outline before you revise, and we can review it together on Tuesday.
But the chapter needs a clearer structure and more evidence in section three.
Thank you for sending the draft chapter, and I can see the effort you have put in.
quests.hint: Acknowledge effort, identify strengths and problems, propose a plan.
quests.explanation: Feedback should give direction, not just judgment. A small next step (a one-page outline) is realistic and motivating.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Piece together an email recommending a colleague for an award.
options: Dear Awards Committee,
Subject: Nomination of Leila Yeboah for the Team Excellence Award
I would like to nominate Leila Yeboah, our customer service lead, for this year's Team Excellence Award.

Over the past year, she reduced complaint response times by 40% and trained twelve new staff, and her calm leadership during the March system outage kept our customers informed.

I would be happy to provide further evidence.

Yours faithfully,
Francis Doyle
quests.hint: Nominee and award, evidence with numbers, offer of more information.
quests.explanation: A nomination is persuasive when it presents specific achievements. Numbers and a named event are more convincing than general praise.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Thank you for the past year / Dear Dr Okoye, / With warm regards, Juliana). Arrange the body.
options: Last month I presented to the board for the first time.
I hope we can keep in touch, and I would be delighted to take you to lunch to say thank you in person.
Your advice to speak up in meetings changed how I work.
As our mentoring year ends, I wanted to write to thank you properly.
quests.hint: Purpose, specific impact, an invitation.
quests.explanation: Specific results (presenting to the board) show real impact. An invitation to keep in touch extends the relationship.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: CAPSTONE 1 of 3 (warm, personal): Your former teacher helped you through a hard year, and you have just graduated. Structure the email you would send.
options: Subject: I graduated, and I wanted you to know why

I don't think I ever thanked you properly, so: thank you. I would love to buy you a coffee whenever you're free.

With love and gratitude,
Nneka
When I nearly left school in Year 11, you spent your lunch breaks helping me catch up, and you never made me feel like a burden.

Dear Mr Achebe,

I graduated on Friday with a degree in engineering, and the first person I wanted to tell was you.
quests.hint: This is a personal email: warm, specific and sincere without being long.
quests.explanation: Warmth comes from specifics such as the lunch breaks, not from big words. The invitation gives the thanks somewhere to go.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: CAPSTONE 2 of 3 (formal, firm): A bank has ignored a complaint. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Formal complaint: unresolved charge of £180, account ending 4471 / Dear Complaints Team, / Yours faithfully, Samuel Zamora). Arrange the body.
options: If I do not receive a reply, I will refer the matter to the Financial Ombudsman Service.
Please refund the charge or explain it in writing within fourteen days, as required by your complaints procedure.
I would prefer to resolve this directly with you.
I am writing to make a formal complaint about a charge of £180 applied on 3 March, which I have queried three times, on 5, 12 and 20 March, without a reply.
quests.hint: Facts and dates, the requested action and deadline, the next step, the preference for resolution.
quests.explanation: This combines what the course has taught: a clear record, a reasonable deadline, a stated consequence and a courteous close.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: CAPSTONE 3 of 3 (upward, bad news under pressure): A key launch will slip by a month. The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Launch moving from 15 October to 14 November: options and recommendation / Dear Ms Aguilar, / Kind regards, Adaora Nwosu). Arrange the body.
options: Launching on time would risk failed payments on day one, and the customer support team could not cope with the volume.
I am writing to tell you that we can no longer launch on 15 October, and I recommend moving to 14 November.
The alternative is to launch without payments on 15 October and add them later, but I do not advise it. Could we speak tomorrow, before I brief the client?
Testing found a fault in the payment system that needs three weeks to fix safely.
quests.hint: Decision needed and recommendation first, cause, alternative, timing of next conversation.
quests.explanation: This is the most demanding kind of upward email: bad news, a recommendation, an alternative you reject, and a clear request. Each part helps a busy director decide quickly and with confidence.
